experiment: AUD-06: statistical simulation and robustness suite for M3-3 DvP
declaredAt: 2026-11-25, before any simulation in this suite was run. Acceptance criteria are not changed after results; a change would be a new version with its reason.
purpose: Do Arbit's actual estimators and its complete development-selection-validation-decision procedure behave correctly when the true defensive signal is known? Results qualify, never change, the frozen 2026 methodology (§5.4).

code.actualImplementations: Every estimator and rule is Arbit's own code, unmodified: walkforward.prepare, fit_fold, metrics, decide; shadow.scheduled_targets, walk_targets, forecast_only, attach_labels; explore.make_extra (rolling 3/5/8, split-half k) and make_opportunity_extra (volume, efficiency, both); lab.adjust, groups, reml_components, bootstrap_components; reliability.halves, split_half; opportunity.reliability; the development selection _select of scripts/model/dvp.py; decisions.units, pairs, metrics, decide; league.decide, summarize.

league.schedule: Every team plays every week (16 games a week) except where a scenario says otherwise; the first game of each week is Thursday night (the preweek cutoff); results are available at 12:00 UTC the next day, as in the real data.

positions.orientation: Offensive positions: points allowed by the defense (the studied unit is the defense). D/ST: points the D/ST scores, driven by the opposing offense's vulnerability (the studied unit is the offense), as in the real observations.

dataGeneratingProcess.points: y = mu_p + a(side, season) + d(studied unit, season, week) + e_nontd + e_td. nontd = y - e_td - td_mean: the defensive trait d lives entirely in the non-touchdown part; e_td is pure noise (touchdown variance).
dataGeneratingProcess.trait: d ~ N(0, sd_d) per studied unit and season; sd_d = noiseSd / sqrt(k_true), so k_true = noise variance / trait variance per game (the quantity REML estimates). k_true = infinity means sd_d = 0.
dataGeneratingProcess.persistence: Across seasons both a and d follow an AR(1) with correlation rho (base 0.5): x_s = rho x_{s-1} + sqrt(1 - rho^2) z.
dataGeneratingProcess.volume: Per cell: volume ~ max(1, N(v_p, 0.25 v_p)) with v_p = mu_p / 1.5; efficiency = y / volume, so points = volume x efficiency exactly (the opportunity estimators' identity). In SIM-14 the trait enters through volume or through efficiency only.
dataGeneratingProcess.oracle: The true conditional mean mu_p + a + d (known only to the simulation): a research reference, never an eligible input.

SIM-05.name: Abrupt midseason change
SIM-05.violation: the trait is redrawn independently at week 9 of every season

SIM-06.name: Gradual drift
SIM-06.violation: the trait follows a within-season AR(1) with weekly correlation 0.85 (stationary sd as SIM-04)

SIM-07.name: Unequal exposure
SIM-07.violation: each team-season loses 0-6 of its games at random (status invalid), so units differ in games observed

SIM-08.name: Random missing
SIM-08.violation: 15% of cells missing completely at random

SIM-09.name: Informative missing
SIM-09.violation: cells whose noise exceeds one sd are missing with probability 0.5 (not at random)

SIM-10.name: Correlated errors
SIM-10.violation: a game shock shared by both sides and positions (sd 0.4 x noise sd) and a league-wide week shock (sd 0.3 x noise sd)

SIM-11.name: Heavy tails
SIM-11.violation: noise is Student t with 3 degrees of freedom, scaled to the same variance

SIM-12.name: Unequal schedule
SIM-12.violation: teams in 4 strength tiers by side strength play 60% of games within their tier

SIM-15.name: Placebo and shuffled-opponent controls
SIM-15.measure: B09 controls' development improvement and selection

SIM-16.name: Multiple competing null predictors
SIM-16.measure: family-wise false candidacy and promotion across positions and estimator families

SIM-17.name: Small-sample league-constrained evaluation
SIM-17.measure: 8 teams, 11 weeks: power, false positives and interval coverage of the cumulative B06-minus-B00 points

SIM-18.name: Zero-change weeks and shared manager decisions
SIM-18.measure: coverage of the changed-weeks and all-weeks bootstraps and a naive decision-level bootstrap

E1.what: Estimator recovery per position and season: REML (lab.reml_components on leave-one-out adjusted unit frames), split-half r and Spearman-Brown k (reliability.halves/split_half), season-cluster bootstrap interval of k (lab.bootstrap_components).
E1.data: Seven seasons (the development span) per repetition.

E2.what: The complete procedure: development folds 2017-2023 (each fit on earlier seasons), the development selection, validation 2024, holdout 2025, walkforward.decide at 1%; Phase C (decisions) on D/ST in all three periods at 1.8 points; every frozen and exploratory variant plus the oracle.
E2.note: Selection and decide use point estimates only, so the metrics bootstrap inside E2 is reduced to 50 replicates (it does not affect any label); interval coverage is studied in U.

E3.what: SIM-17 and SIM-18 with league.decide and league.summarize: an 8-team league, 2 D/STs held per team (5 teams) or 1 (3 teams), 18 free agents, 11 weeks; forecasts with a known correlation to the true points (B00 rho 0.15; B06 rho 0.15 under the null, 0.22 under the alternative).

U.what: Interval coverage of walkforward.metrics' block bootstrap of the RMSE difference, with a known true difference: y = s + e, forecast A = 0, forecast B = c s, so the population RMSE difference is exact.
conditions: temporal AR(1) across weeks, week blocks
U.deviation: 1,000 instead of the frozen 2,000 replicates per interval, for budget; Monte Carlo error of a quantile at 1,000 is small relative to the coverage question.

randomStreams: numpy SeedSequence(20261125) spawned per experiment, scenario and repetition; each repetition spawns separate children for data generation, the walk's own seed (Settings.seed, used by B09 controls), permutations, and bootstrap seeds.
measurements: True and estimated signal and noise variance, reliability and k; bias, variance and MSE of log k; boundary and non-convergence rates; interval coverage and width; forecast RMSE and MAE per variant and the oracle; incremental improvement over B00; candidate selection and the selected family; Phase B and Phase C labels; false positive, power, correct rejection, correct candidate recovery and false promotion frequencies; winner's curse (development minus validation improvement of the selected variant); Monte Carlo standard errors on every frequency.

acceptance.A1: Null (SIM-01): Phase B PROMISING at most 5% per position, and Phase B and Phase C both PROMISING for D/ST at most 5%.
acceptance.A2: Multiple nulls (SIM-16): any of six positions PROMISING at most 10%.
acceptance.A3: Strong signal (SIM-04): D/ST Phase B PROMISING at least 80%. Moderate and weak reported.
acceptance.A4: k recovery (E1): for k_true 8 and 20 with independent normal noise, median |k_hat / k_true - 1| at most 0.25 and REML convergence at least 95%. Null: share of unidentified k (infinite or boundary) reported.
acceptance.A5: Candidate recovery (SIM-04): the selected variant is a shrunk one (b03, b03r, b04, b05, b06, b07 families) in at least 90% of repetitions where a candidate is selected.
acceptance.A6: Controls (SIM-15): each B09 control cuts development RMSE by 1% in at most 5% of repetitions, null and signal.
acceptance.A7: Coverage (U): 92-98% where the bootstrap block matches the dependence and there are at least 10 blocks; other conditions reported as limitations.
acceptance.A8: League (SIM-17/18): under the null the all-weeks interval excludes zero at most 7%; its coverage of the true expected gain 90-98%.

inconclusive: A criterion is INCONCLUSIVE when its Monte Carlo 95% interval straddles the threshold, or when more than 5% of a scenario's repetitions fail to run (each failure is recorded).

budget.wallClock: at most 6 hours on this PC
budget.rule: If a pilot of 5 repetitions per E2 scenario predicts more than the budget, E2 repetitions are reduced uniformly to no fewer than 200 and the reduction is recorded. No other reduction is allowed.

frozenMethodology: Unchanged whatever the results. A material defect is recorded and escalated, never silently corrected in the ongoing 2026 experiment (§5.4).
